chart_references: Yet the rush to build port infrastructure is likely to result in huge inefficiencies (see chart). Many investors, including both American and Chinese taxpayers, will see disappointing returns. And political pressure for shipping firms to use particular ports and sea routes, in defiance of all commercial logic, is bound to grow.

extraction.title: Shipping
extraction.subtitle: The global scramble for ports The investment frenzy is driven by anxiety about China’s tightening grip on supply chains
extraction.summary: The global competition for port control is intensifying, driven by geopolitical tensions, particularly between the U.S. and China. Investments in port infrastructure are expected to rise significantly, but this rush may lead to inefficiencies and political pressures affecting shipping routes. China's dominance in global ports is causing concern among Western nations, prompting them to bolster their own maritime capabilities.
